## Changes since 9.3.0-dzbarsky20

- Filter native toolchain declarations by the target platform before configuring their settings. Debug mode still analyzes every declaration for rejection diagnostics. Configurable aliases, invalid constraints, cycles, and declarations that inherit target platform constraints retain normal analysis; errors in irrelevant declarations can be deferred until their type and platform constraints are requested. Based on [dzbarsky/bazel#10](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/10).
- Weakly intern identical `ConfigMatchingProvider` values across configurations, including their match results and diagnostics. Based on [dzbarsky/bazel#12](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/12).
- Weakly intern the complete provider map of native `config_setting` targets when the map has no `NativeInfo`. Maps with `NativeInfo` stay distinct to preserve configuration-specific coverage data. Based on [dzbarsky/bazel#11](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/11).

The original PR #12 benchmark reported 317 MB less retained heap with a 0.80% higher median analysis time across three interleaved partial analyses. PR #11 reported another 62 MB less retained heap in one comparison with PR #12 already applied. These are separate measurements, not a combined release benchmark; neither establishes a peak-RSS or analysis-time improvement for this release.

### Validation

Six targeted Bazel test suites passed on the combined branch: `ConfigRulesTests`, `SelectTests`, `PlatformAnalysisTests`, `ConfigurableAttributesTest`, `RuleConfiguredTargetTest`, and `RegisteredToolchainsFunctionTest`.

### Release publication

This release is immutable and includes Linux and macOS binaries for x86_64 and arm64, with SHA-256 checksums and build-provenance attestations.
